annotations.text:
Lilo — light, with the flows and gestures worked out.

On Grok Bot: there is no separate app under that name in Mobbin's index. Every result returns Grok, so they are the same thing. Searching it again did turn up more of it — the bold lead sentence before the prose, Day 1 style subheads, the model-and-time stamp under an answer, an audio bar that slides in above the composer, and the composer turning black with a Stop while it generates. Ask and Add now follow that.

Light throughout, which is where three of the four sources actually live. Luma's real trick was never the darkness but the tint — the cover's own colours washed softly behind the content — and that works on white.

Two new boards below the screens. Three flows counted step by step against how they work today, and every gesture with the visible control that does the same job. No gesture is the only way to reach anything.

Filing a confirmation goes from nine steps to three. Getting a yes from four people moves inside the app. Working out the money stops being a separate chore, because the costs arrive attached to the bookings.

Gestures are shortcuts for things done repeatedly — voting on six places, ticking a packing list, chasing three people. Paying, settling and cancelling deliberately keep their buttons: anything a toast cannot undo should cost a deliberate tap.
The orange notes drawn on Home, The plan, Saved, The kitty, Settle up, Add and Manage are annotations for you, not app furniture. Each marks a gesture and names the tap that does the same job.
